This change is pretty large. In the future, consider breaking it up into smaller commits if you can. For example, the utility.*pp changes could have been a separate commit.

It just makes it easier for you to test and reviewers to review.

Sorry, my previous comment was not very clear. You don't need to break *this* commit into smaller ones. But for future work, use smaller commits if possible. I know sometimes that is hard due to a bunch of inter-related changes.

I agree that this path is kind of strange since it has both 'power_supplies' and 'psus' in it.

However, this is used in several other places, such as:
* https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-power/blob/master/types.hpp#L48
* https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/blob/master/chassis_state_manager.cpp#L87

This path is how the PSU app communicates that a brownout is occurring to other applications.

So you need to either leave it the same or change those other places too.
Restored to previous code
Do callbacks like this need to check if the chassis is present before continuing?
Done
Done

This is going to get called once per second by analyze(), right?

We should not be polling the D-Bus property value. This is going to cause a lot of expensive D-Bus traffic.

From the commit comments, I thought the plan was to remove the Chassis object completely if it is not present.

If I misunderstood and the Chassis object will remain, then it should have an isPresent data member. That should be set and updated using the normal D-Bus pattern of
- Get the D-Bus property value during initialization if it is available on D-Bus
- Add an InterfacesAdded listener to cover case where property is published on D-Bus later
- Add a PropertiesChanged listener for when the value changes

This is not a backplane path if the interface is supportedConfIntf right?

The supported configuration information is in the EM chassis object. The PSU information is in the EM backplane object.

This method is getting pretty long and complex.

It looks like from the code on lines 98-103 that the return value from getChassisAssociation() is a chassis inventory path + an extra node.

Should getChassisAssociation remove the extra node so the calling code can be simpler?

I don't understand this.

If a chassis is not present, why do you remove it if exists in the list, but you add it if it doesn't exist in the list?

Wouldn't you want it to either always be in the list or never be in the list?
no more chassis remove/add
I'm not sure what this journal message means, but it is in the block of code for when a PSU interface was found. So no PSU configuration interfaces may have been found.
Acknowledged

I believe this callback is getting called when *any* inventory item has a change in their Item interface, right?

It could be a chassis, PSU, DIMM, fan, etc.

All of those inventory paths may have 'chassis' in the middle of their path, like

```
/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/fan0
```

So I don't think this check is going to return when the item is not a chassis if that was your intent.
removed from ChassisManager

I believe for some systems the present property is initially set to false for all chassis. Then GPIOs or other means are used to detect which chassis are present, and the property changes to true.

If the PSU app starts before the process above is done, you might see a chassis go from not present to present, but it was never really gone.

So in your journal message, you may want to say "Chassis present" rather than "Chassis returned".
Done
